question_text: Among bryophytes, lichens and ferns, which one is a pioneer species in a xeric succession?

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya Junior Fastrack botany section, Chapter 13, book p.35, VSAQ 2. The book prints the one-word answer 'Lichens'; the reason and the order of stages are added here from standard ecology. Only one source book is held for botany — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand is physics-only and no botany board paper is in the corpus — so the two-book union check and the back-test are both structurally impossible for this card, not merely unrun. steps.label: The answer
lines: Lichens are the pioneer species of a xeric
A xeric succession starts on a bare, dry
surface such as a rock, where there is no
steps.why: The pioneer is whichever organism can live where nothing else can. On bare dry rock only a lichen can hold on, so it forms the first stage.
common_mistakes: Answering bryophytes. Mosses form the second stage here, after lichens have made some soil.
Answering ferns. Ferns need soil and appear much later.
steps.memory_tip: On bare rock the first stage is lichen. Moss follows only after there is some soil.
steps.margin_note: The single word Lichens carries the first mark. Add the habitat sentence for safety.

steps.label: Why lichens
lines: Lichens grow on bare rock and release acids
that break the rock into fine particles.
Their dead remains mix with those particles
and form the first thin layer of soil.
steps.why: Lichens are pioneers because they produce the soil that the next stages need. Stating the sequence shows the examiner the answer is understood, not guessed.
common_mistakes: Writing the sequence backwards, with trees before shrubs.
Calling a lichen a plant. A lichen is an alga and a fungus living together.
steps.memory_tip: Small to tall: lichen, moss, herb, shrub, tree.
steps.margin_note: One reason line plus the sequence completes a two-mark answer.

insider_note: One word answers the question, but examiners in this chapter reward the sequence line. Writing lichens, mosses, herbs, shrubs, trees in order rarely loses a mark.
